Alyssa - CS: Heads-up — drafting a customer update for a hardware fault in eu-west1 Dedicated pool. Need quick sign-off on tone and technical accuracy. Short summary below, then proposed message.
Mike - Infra: Thanks. Can you add exact trigger (ECC/Xid thresholds) and whether any live workloads were dropped? Customers will ask for specifics.
Alyssa - CS: Good call. Preliminary: one rack (4 nodes) saw repeated ECC corrections then an Xid 79 GPU reset on two cards. We drained the affected nodes and routed traffic to spare capacity in-region. No in-flight inference requests were lost — background retries covered the brief reconnections. Impact: ~8% capacity reduction in that Dedicated pool for ~20 minutes during failover. Replacement required RMA on two cards; ETA 48-72h for physical replacement and post-remediation testing.
Raj - SRE: Adding detection/context: our health monitor fires when ECC corrected errors > 1e4 within 24h OR when Xid resets > 3 within 1h. In this case threshold breached for two cards, automatic drain triggered by autoscaler + `gpu-healthd` runbook. Logs snippet below for debugging so customers with deeper infra teams can see root cause markers:
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] GPU0: ECC_CORRECTED=12430 XID_RESET=0
[2026-03-15T08:14:17Z] GPU1: ECC_CORRECTED=9800 XID_RESET=1
[2026-03-15T08:15:22Z] GPU1: XID=79 RESET
[2026-03-15T08:15:25Z] node: cordon -> drain -> scheduler-migration (10 pods)
```
Jordan - Eng Runtime: Please avoid deep kernel-level claims in the customer message. Keep the technical appendix short and offer an optional deeper incident pack. Also confirm whether Private (VPC/on-prem) customers need any manual action — they often do for physical replacements.
Mike - Infra: For Dedicated customers: we should offer a succinct summary + timeline + mitigations + SLA credit language. For Private customers: explain we can ship replacement cards or coordinate an on-site swap; include a maintenance window suggestion. Also include escalation contact (private-dedicated@redwood.com) and a link to our runbook.
Alyssa - CS: Proposed customer-facing message (concise):
"Hello — we want to let you know about a recent GPU hardware issue that affected customers using Dedicated capacity in eu-west1. On 2026-03-15 we detected elevated ECC correction counts on two GPUs which subsequently triggered automatic node draining and failover to spare capacity. During the failover period (approx. 20 minutes) some capacity in your Dedicated pool was temporarily reduced; no in-flight requests were lost and request retries resumed as normal. We have initiated hardware replacement (RMA) for the affected GPUs; physical replacement and verification are expected within 48–72 hours.

What we did: automatic detection -> immediate node drain -> live reroute to spare capacity -> RMA & post-repair validation.

What this means for you: brief capacity dip during the failover window; no action required on your side for Hosted Dedicated. If you operate a Private/on-prem deployment, our field ops team will contact your designated admin to schedule the hardware swap and any required maintenance window.

Remediation & follow-up: we will share a post-remediation note when replacements complete. If you experienced degraded performance beyond the 20-minute window, please reply or open a support ticket and we will prioritize an investigation.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience. If you'd like a technical incident pack, reply and we'll share logs and our diagnostic timeline.

Best,
Redwood Infrastructure/Customer Success Team"
Raj - SRE: Add a single sentence offering SLA credit details: "If this incident caused sustained capacity loss beyond our SLA threshold, you may be eligible for credits per your Dedicated contract; contact support for assessment." Keep it short.
Mike - Infra: Also include an ops contact and JIRA/incident ID so customers can reference it: INC-2026-1197. And a proactive note about capacity: we temporarily bumped autoscaler headroom and verified other racks in the region for early warning.
Alyssa - CS: Updated one-line for SLA + incident ID inserted. Final ask: can engineering confirm the 48–72h estimate? If so I'll send as customer blast and post to status.redwood.ai.
Jordan - Eng Runtime: 48–72h is fine for sourcing and bench testing replacement cards; mark as "estimated". Also add: "we will not change model weights or touch customer data during hardware ops" — customers worry about data plane changes.
ops-bot: [automated] Scheduled hardware replacement job created: job_id=hw-repl-8234, window=2026-03-16T09:00Z -> 2026-03-17T17:00Z (ETA subject to courier). :white_check_mark:
Alyssa - CS: Perfect. I'll send the customer-facing note now and open the incident pack for any customers that request it. Thanks all. :wave:
